source.text: Οὐ περὶ τούτων δὲ ἐρωτῶ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τῶν πιστευόντων διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτῶν εἰς ἐμέ, ἵνα πάντες ἓν ὦσιν, καθὼς σύ, πάτερ, ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν σοί, ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἡμῖν ὦσιν, ἵνα ὁ κόσμος πιστεύῃ ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.

records.literal_gloss: Not concerning these but I ask only, but also concerning the [ones] believing through the word of them into me, \v 21 that all one may be, just as you, Father, in me and I in you, that also they in us may be, that the world may believe that you me sent.

en.L: And I am not asking on behalf of these only, but also on behalf of those who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through their word, \v 21 that all may be one, just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Father, [are] in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and I in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, that they also may be in {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}, so that the world may believe that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: I am not asking on behalf of these alone. My prayer is also for those who are going to believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} through their message. \v 21 Father, I ask that all of them may be one. Just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and I am in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, so may they too be in {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}, so that the world may come to believe that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I am not praying only for these disciples. I am also praying for all who will believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} because of their message. \v 21 Father, I pray that all of them will be one, just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and I am in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I pray that they will be in {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}} too. Then the world will believe that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Or je ne prie pas seulement au sujet de ceux-ci, mais aussi au sujet de ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} par leur parole, \v 21 afin que tous soient un, comme {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Père, [{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es] en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, afin qu’eux aussi soient en {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}}, afin que le monde croie que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé.
fr.B: Je ne prie pas seulement pour ceux-ci. Ma prière est aussi pour ceux qui vont croire en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} grâce à leur message. \v 21 Père, je demande que tous soient un. Comme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et que je suis en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, qu’eux aussi soient en {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}}, pour que le monde en vienne à croire que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé.
fr.R: Je ne prie pas seulement pour ces disciples. Je prie aussi pour tous ceux qui croiront en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} grâce à leur message. \v 21 Père, je prie pour qu’ils soient tous un, comme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et comme je suis en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Je prie pour qu’ils soient en {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}}, eux aussi. Alors le monde croira que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé.

vi.L: Và Con không chỉ cầu xin cho những người này, nhưng cũng cho những người nhờ lời của họ mà tin vào Con, \v 21 để tất cả đều là một; lạy Cha, như Cha [ở] trong Con và Con trong Cha, để họ cũng ở trong chúng ta, hầu cho thế gian tin rằng Cha đã sai Con.
vi.B: Con không chỉ cầu xin cho những người này mà thôi, nhưng cũng cho những người sẽ tin vào Con nhờ lời rao giảng của họ. \v 21 Lạy Cha, Con xin cho tất cả đều được hiệp một. Như Cha ở trong Con và Con ở trong Cha, xin cho họ cũng ở trong Cha và Con, để thế gian tin rằng Cha đã sai Con.
vi.R: Con không chỉ cầu nguyện cho các môn đồ này. Con cũng cầu nguyện cho tất cả những người sẽ tin vào Con nhờ lời rao giảng của họ. \v 21 Lạy Cha, Con cầu xin cho tất cả họ được hiệp một, như Cha ở trong Con và Con ở trong Cha. Con cầu xin cho họ cũng ở trong Cha và Con. Như vậy thế gian sẽ tin rằng Cha đã sai Con.

ko.L: 그리고 제가 청하는 것은 이들만을 위해서가 아니라, 이들의 말을 통하여 저를 믿는 사람들을 위해서이기도 합니다. \v 21 [이는] 모두가 하나가 되게 하려는 것입니다. 아버지, 아버지께서 제 안에 [계시고] 제가 아버지 안에 있는 것처럼, 그들도 우리 안에 있게 하려는 것이며, 세상이 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 믿게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 제가 이들만을 위하여 청하는 것이 아닙니다. 이들이 전하는 말을 듣고 저를 믿게 될 사람들을 위해서도 청합니다. \v 21 아버지, 그들이 모두 하나가 되게 해 주십시오. 아버지께서 제 안에 계시고 제가 아버지 안에 있는 것처럼, 그들도 우리 안에 있게 해 주십시오. 그래서 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 세상이 믿게 해 주십시오.
ko.R: 저는 이 제자들만을 위해 기도하는 것이 아닙니다. 이들이 전하는 말을 듣고 저를 믿게 될 모든 사람들을 위해서도 기도합니다. \v 21 아버지, 그들이 모두 하나가 되게 해 주십시오. 아버지께서 제 안에 계시고 제가 아버지 안에 있는 것처럼 하나가 되게 해 주십시오. 그들도 우리 안에 있게 해 주십시오. 그러면 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 세상이 믿을 것입니다.

alignments.target_span: those who are going to believe

decisions.choice: those who believe in me through their word: the people who will come to believe through the disciples' message
alternatives: only those who already believed at the time
decisions.reason: The participle πιστευόντων is present, "the believing ones", but it is defined by "through their word": the word of the disciples Jesus has just been praying for (17:6-19), whom he is sending into the world (17:18). So Jesus's prayer reaches beyond the Eleven to all who will believe through their witness (compare 20:29, 31). "Their word" is the disciples' message about Jesus, which is his own word passed on (17:8, 14).

decisions.choice: one: neuter, "one thing", a unity of many persons, not one person
decisions.reason: "All" (πάντες) is masculine plural, but "one" (ἓν) is neuter, as when Jesus says "I and the Father are one" (10:30). The many believers do not become one person or lose who they are; they are made one, as the Father and the Son are two and yet one (17:11, 22).

decisions.choice: the unity is modelled on, and drawn from, the unity of the Father and the Son: believers are one by being in the Father and the Son
alternatives: agreement of opinion or purpose only
a hidden, inward unity that the world cannot see
decisions.reason: The pattern is "just as you, Father, are in me and I in you": the Father and the Son live in each other. Jesus then asks that believers "also may be in us", so their oneness with each other comes from their sharing in that life (14:20; 15:4-5). It is not mere agreement, and it is not only invisible either: it is to be seen, so that the world may believe (compare 13:34-35, where the world knows his disciples by their love for one another). The passage does not say what outward form this unity takes.

decisions.choice: the first two "that" clauses say what Jesus asks; the third gives the purpose of it all, that the world may believe
alternatives: each "that" clause depends on the one before it, a chain of purposes
the second "that" clause gives the purpose of the "just as" clause
decisions.reason: The sentence has three clauses with ἵνα. The first two say much the same thing and are best read as the content of Jesus's request: that all may be one, and, put more fully, that they may be in the Father and the Son. The third states what the request is for: that the world may believe. The same shape returns in 17:22-23. The word can introduce either the content of a request or its purpose, so the links between the clauses are not certain; the meaning of the whole is not much affected.

decisions.choice: that they also may be in us, as the SBLGNT reads
alternatives: that they also may be one in us (Codex Sinaiticus and most later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "one" here, "that they also may be one in us", which repeats the "one" of the clause before. Some important early manuscripts, among them Codex Vaticanus, do not have it, and the SBLGNT follows them. The addition is easy to explain as a copyist making the two clauses match. The sense is close either way. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity that does not yet believe, which may still come to believe
alternatives: humanity set against God, with no hope of believing
decisions.reason: In this prayer "the world" is often the human world that hates Jesus and his disciples (17:14, 25). Here, as in 3:16-17, it is the same world seen as the object of God's mission: the unity of believers is meant to lead it to believe that the Father sent the Son.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:we|We}}, {{deity_pronoun:us|Us}}
decisions.reason: John 17 is a prayer to the Father, so every "you" and "your" spoken to him uses the deity_pronoun setting, as do "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself, and "we" and "us" for the Father and the Son together (as in 14:23). "I" takes no span. This applies throughout the passage. "They", "them" and "all" are plural and need no gender setting.

decisions.choice: asking on behalf of (L, B); praying for (R); who are going to believe (B), who will believe (R); word (L), message (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means "ask", and with this preposition "ask on behalf of"; "asking for these" would sound as if Jesus were asking to be given them. Readable says "praying", which is what the asking is. Balanced and Readable say "are going to believe" and "will believe", since those meant are people who will come to believe later (meaning decision m1), and "message" for the disciples' "word", so that it is not taken as a single word.

decisions.choice: My prayer is also for, I ask that, so may they (B); these disciples, I pray that, Then (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long sentence and repeat that Jesus is asking or praying, so that each "that" clause is plainly part of his request (meaning decision m4). Readable names "these disciples" and says "Then" for the clause of purpose. Both move "Father" to the start of the request, where English puts an address.

decisions.choice: speech tenses: passé composé for the Greek aorist and perfect at every level ("tu m’as envoyé", "je leur ai fait connaître"), present for the present ("je prie"), future for the future
alternatives: passé simple for the aorists at Literal
decisions.reason: The whole passage (17:20-26) is Jesus's prayer, with no narration; the French brief puts speech in the passé composé at every level, as people speak to God.

decisions.choice: je prie (pour, au sujet de) (L, B, R); Ma prière est aussi pour (B)
decisions.reason: As in 17:9: the verb means asking on someone's behalf, and French "prier pour" says that plainly at every level.

decisions.choice: "Cha" for the Father and "Con" for Jesus; "chúng ta" (L), "Cha và Con" (B, R) for "us"; no setting spans
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for John 17, recorded once in this passage: Jesus speaks to the Father as a son. "Cha" and "Con" are capitalised nouns and take no deity_pronoun setting. Where the Greek has "we" or "us" for the Father and the Son, Literal keeps the inclusive "chúng ta" and Balanced and Readable name them.

decisions.choice: lời rao giảng (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Lời của họ" alone could mean any of their words; "lời rao giảng" says that it is the message they proclaim.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by the honorific -si-, 께서 and 그분 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: Verse 21's "that" clauses become their own sentence, opened by a bracketed [이는]
alternatives: one sentence running across the verse marker
decisions.reason: Korean puts a purpose clause before its main verb, so keeping one sentence would move verse 21's words into verse 20; a new sentence keeps each verse's content after its marker.

decisions.choice: 말 (L); 전하는 말 (B, R) for the disciples' "word"
decisions.reason: 말씀 is kept for God's word and Jesus's; the disciples' message is their 말, which Balanced and Readable make clear with 전하는.

source.text: κἀγὼ τὴν δόξαν ἣν δέδωκάς μοι δέδωκα αὐτοῖς, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν καθὼς ἡμεῖς ἕν, ἐγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ σὺ ἐν ἐμοί, ἵνα ὦσιν τετελειωμένοι εἰς ἕν, ἵνα γινώσκῃ ὁ κόσμος ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας καὶ ἠγάπησας αὐτοὺς καθὼς ἐμὲ ἠγάπησας.

records.literal_gloss: And I the glory which you have given to me have given to them, that they may be one just as we one, \v 23 I in them and you in me, that they may be having been perfected into one, that may know the world that you me sent and loved them just as me you loved.

en.L: And the glory that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I have given to them, so that they may be one just as {{deity_pronoun:we|We}} [are] one, \v 23 I in them and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so that they may be perfected into one, so that the world may know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and loved them just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: The glory that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I have given to them, so that they may be one just as {{deity_pronoun:we|We}} are one. \v 23 I am in them and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So may they be brought to perfect oneness, and the world will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and loved them just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I have given them the glory that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so that they may be one, just as {{deity_pronoun:we|We}} are one. \v 23 I am in them, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. May they be made completely one. Then the world will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. It will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love them just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, la gloire que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnée, je la leur ai donnée, afin qu’ils soient un comme {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}} [sommes] un, \v 23 {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en eux et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, afin qu’ils soient rendus parfaits dans l’unité, afin que le monde sache que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as aimés comme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as aimé.
fr.B: La gloire que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnée, je la leur ai donnée, pour qu’ils soient un comme {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}} sommes un. \v 23 Je suis en eux et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Qu’ils soient ainsi conduits à une unité parfaite, et le monde saura que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as aimés comme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as aimé.
fr.R: Je leur ai donné la gloire que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnée, pour qu’ils soient un, comme {{deity_pronoun:nous|Nous}} sommes un. \v 23 Je suis en eux, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Que leur unité soit complète ! Alors le monde saura que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé. Il saura que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les aimes comme {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimes.

vi.L: Và vinh quang Cha đã ban cho Con, Con đã ban cho họ, để họ là một như chúng ta là một, \v 23 Con ở trong họ và Cha ở trong Con, để họ được làm cho trọn vẹn nên một, hầu cho thế gian biết rằng Cha đã sai Con và đã yêu thương họ như Cha đã yêu thương Con.
vi.B: Vinh quang Cha đã ban cho Con, Con đã ban cho họ, để họ được hiệp một như Cha và Con là một. \v 23 Con ở trong họ và Cha ở trong Con. Như vậy, xin cho họ được hiệp một trọn vẹn, và thế gian sẽ biết rằng Cha đã sai Con và đã yêu thương họ như Cha đã yêu thương Con.
vi.R: Con đã ban cho họ vinh quang Cha đã ban cho Con, để họ được hiệp một, như Cha và Con là một. \v 23 Con ở trong họ, và Cha ở trong Con. Xin cho họ được hoàn toàn hiệp một. Khi đó thế gian sẽ biết rằng Cha đã sai Con. Thế gian sẽ biết rằng Cha yêu thương họ như Cha yêu thương Con.

ko.L: 그리고 아버지께서 저에게 주신 영광을 제가 그들에게 주었습니다. 이는 우리가 하나인 것처럼 그들도 하나가 되게 하려는 것입니다. \v 23 곧 제가 그들 안에 있고 아버지께서 제 안에 계셔서, 그들이 온전하게 되어 하나를 이루게 하려는 것이며, 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것과 저를 사랑하신 것처럼 그들도 사랑하셨다는 것을 세상이 알게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 아버지께서 저에게 주신 영광을 저도 그들에게 주었습니다. 우리가 하나인 것처럼 그들도 하나가 되게 하려는 것입니다. \v 23 제가 그들 안에 있고 아버지께서 제 안에 계십니다. 그리하여 그들이 온전히 하나가 되게 해 주십시오. 그러면 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것과, 저를 사랑하신 것처럼 그들도 사랑하셨다는 것을 세상이 알게 될 것입니다.
ko.R: 저는 아버지께서 저에게 주신 영광을 그들에게 주었습니다. 우리가 하나인 것처럼 그들도 하나가 되게 하려는 것입니다. \v 23 제가 그들 안에 있고, 아버지께서 제 안에 계십니다. 그들이 완전히 하나가 되게 해 주십시오. 그러면 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 세상이 알게 될 것입니다. 또 아버지께서 저를 사랑하시는 것처럼 그들도 사랑하신다는 것을 알게 될 것입니다.

decisions.choice: the glory: the Father's own presence and life shown in the Son, which the Son shares with his own and which makes them one
alternatives: the glory of the age to come, still to be given
the honor of suffering and dying as Jesus does
decisions.reason: John does not say what this glory is, and the reading is uncertain. In this Gospel glory is God himself made known: the Word made his home among us and "we saw his glory" (1:14), and Jesus showed it in his signs (2:11). The Father gave it to the Son (17:5, 24), and the Son has given it to his disciples in what he has made known to them (17:6-8), so that they share his life with the Father; this is why it leads to their being one. The perfect "have given" speaks of something already done. Others take it as the glory they will see and share in the age to come (17:24); others connect it with the cross, where Jesus is glorified (12:23-24; 13:31), or with the Spirit, given when he is glorified (7:39).

decisions.choice: one just as we are one: the neuter "one" again, with the oneness of Father and Son as its pattern
decisions.reason: Both times "one" (ἓν, ἕν) is neuter, as in 17:21 and 10:30, and "we" is the Father and the Son. The Greek leaves out the verb in "just as we one".

decisions.choice: I in them and you in me: says how they are to be one; the Son in them and the Father in the Son joins them to the Father
alternatives: the start of a new thought, going with what follows
decisions.reason: These words have no verb and stand between two "that" clauses. They are best read as explaining the oneness just named: the Son lives in believers and the Father in the Son, so believers are bound to the Father through the Son, and to one another (14:20; 15:4-5). They also lead into what follows, since being made one rests on this indwelling.

decisions.choice: perfected into one: brought to completion as one, a unity that reaches its full goal, by God's doing
decisions.reason: The verb τετελειωμένοι means to bring to completion or to the goal; Jesus uses it of finishing the work the Father gave him (4:34; 5:36; 17:4). It is passive, so this is something God does in them, and "into one" says what it leads to. 1 John speaks in the same way of love being made complete in those who keep God's word (1 John 2:5; 4:12).

decisions.choice: the world may know that the Father sent the Son and loves the disciples with the same love as the Son
alternatives: loved them in a lesser way than the Son
decisions.reason: As in 17:21, the world here is the human world that may still come to know (meaning decision m6 there). What it is to know is twofold: that the Father sent Jesus, and that the Father has loved the disciples "just as" he loved the Son. Jesus has said the same in 16:27 ("the Father himself loves you"). The aorist "loved" looks at the Father's love as a whole, not at one past moment.

decisions.choice: perfected into one (L); brought to perfect oneness (B); made completely one (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "perfected into one". Balanced says "brought to perfect oneness" to keep both the idea of reaching a goal and the word "one" that runs through 17:21-23 (meaning decision m4); Readable says it plainly. The Literal "we [are] one" brackets the verb the Greek leaves out.

decisions.choice: I am in them and you are in me, So may they ... and the world will know (B); May they ..., Then the world will know ... It will know (R); you love them just as you love me (R)
alternatives: so that they may be ..., so that the world may know (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long sentence and supply the verbs the Greek leaves out in "I in them and you in me" (meaning decision m3). Readable says "Then" for the clause of purpose and repeats "It will know" for the second thing the world is to know. It uses the present "love" because the Father's love for the Son and for the disciples is not over (meaning decision m5); Literal and Balanced keep "loved".

decisions.choice: rendus parfaits dans l’unité (L); conduits à une unité parfaite (B); Que leur unité soit complète (R)
decisions.reason: The passive participle means brought to completion as one, by God's doing (meaning decision m4). French can say "un" after "être", as in verse 22, but not "rendus parfaits en un"; the noun "unité" keeps the sense of one whole at each level, and Balanced and Readable keep the passive or the wish of the Greek.

decisions.choice: hiệp một (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Hiệp một" (be joined as one) says a unity of many persons, which the neuter "one" of the Greek means; "là một" could be read as becoming one person. Literal keeps the bare "là một".

decisions.choice: 온전하게 되어 하나를 이루다 (L); 온전히 하나가 되다 (B); 완전히 하나가 되다 (R) for "perfected into one"
alternatives: 완전하게 되어 하나가 되다 at every level
decisions.reason: 온전 keeps the sense of being brought to completion; Readable uses the more common 완전히.

source.text: πάτερ, ὃ δέδωκάς μοι, θέλω ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ κἀκεῖνοι ὦσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ, ἵνα θεωρῶσιν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἐμὴν ἣν δέδωκάς μοι, ὅτι ἠγάπησάς με πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: Father, what you have given to me, I want that where am I those also may be with me, that they may behold the glory the mine which you have given to me, because you loved me before foundation of world.

en.L: Father, what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: I want that where I am, they also may be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so that they may see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory, which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before [the] foundation of [the] world.
en.B: Father, all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: it is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} will that they too may be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} where I am, to see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory, which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before the world was founded.
en.R: Father, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I want them to be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} where I am. I want them to see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory. You gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} this glory because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before the world was made.

fr.L: Père, ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donné, je veux que là où je suis, eux aussi soient avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, afin qu’ils voient la gloire qui est la {{deity_pronoun:mienne|Mienne}}, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnée, parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as aimé avant [la] fondation du monde.
fr.B: Père, ceux que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnés, {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} volonté est qu’eux aussi soient avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} là où je suis, pour qu’ils voient {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gloire, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donnée parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as aimé avant que le monde soit fondé.
fr.R: Père, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} les as donnés, et je veux qu’ils soient avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} là où je suis. Je veux qu’ils voient {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gloire. Tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as donné cette gloire parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as aimé avant la création du monde.

vi.L: Lạy Cha, những gì Cha đã ban cho Con, Con muốn rằng Con ở đâu thì họ cũng ở với Con tại đó, để họ thấy vinh quang của Con mà Cha đã ban cho Con, vì Cha đã yêu thương Con trước khi đặt nền thế gian.
vi.B: Lạy Cha, tất cả những gì Cha đã ban cho Con, Con muốn họ cũng được ở với Con nơi Con ở, để thấy vinh quang của Con, là vinh quang Cha đã ban cho Con vì Cha đã yêu thương Con trước khi thế gian được dựng nên.
vi.R: Lạy Cha, Cha đã ban họ cho Con, và Con muốn họ được ở với Con nơi Con ở. Con muốn họ thấy vinh quang của Con. Cha đã ban cho Con vinh quang này vì Cha đã yêu thương Con trước khi tạo dựng thế gian.

ko.L: 아버지, 아버지께서 저에게 주신 것, 저는 제가 있는 곳에 그들도 저와 함께 있기를 원합니다. 이는 아버지께서 세상의 기초가 놓이기 전에 저를 사랑하셨기 때문에 저에게 주신 제 영광을 그들이 보게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 아버지, 아버지께서 저에게 주신 모든 사람이 제가 있는 곳에 저와 함께 있기를 저는 원합니다. 그들이 제 영광을 보게 하려는 것입니다. 그 영광은 아버지께서 세상이 세워지기 전부터 저를 사랑하셔서 저에게 주신 것입니다.
ko.R: 아버지, 아버지께서 그들을 저에게 주셨습니다. 저는 그들이 제가 있는 곳에 저와 함께 있기를 원합니다. 그들이 제 영광을 보기를 원합니다. 아버지께서는 세상이 만들어지기 전부터 저를 사랑하셔서, 저에게 이 영광을 주셨습니다.

decisions.choice: what you have given me: the believers as one whole, given by the Father to the Son; then "they" takes up each one of them
alternatives: a thing or task given to the Son
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun ὃ is neuter singular, "what", as in "all that the Father gives me will come to me" (6:37, 39) and "all that you have given him" (17:2). John speaks this way of all who belong to the Son, taken together as the Father's gift. The next words turn to the plural κἀκεῖνοι, "they too", the persons themselves.

decisions.choice: what (neuter singular), as the SBLGNT reads
alternatives: those whom (masculine plural), in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "those whom", which fits the plural "they" that follows and is the easier reading. The neuter is found in important early manuscripts and matches John's way of speaking in 6:37, 39 and 17:2, so it is the more likely original; a copyist was more likely to smooth it than to create it. The sense is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: I want: Jesus states his will, in full accord with the Father, not only a request
decisions.reason: Up to now Jesus has said "I ask" (17:9, 15, 20). Here he says θέλω, "I will" or "I want". The Son speaks with authority (5:21; 21:22), but not against the Father: it is the Father's will that the Son lose none of those given to him and raise them up (6:39-40). So the prayer is also a statement of what Jesus intends.

decisions.choice: to be where Jesus is and to see his glory: the glory he had with the Father before creation, given in love
alternatives: the glory seen during his life on earth
decisions.reason: "Where I am" is with the Father, where Jesus goes to prepare a place for his own (14:2-3; 12:26). There they will see his glory: the glory he had with the Father "before the world existed" (17:5), now given to him as the Son, out of a love older than the world. "The foundation of the world" means its creation. The disciples have seen his glory in part already (1:14); here they will see it fully. The verb θεωρῶσιν means to look at, to see with attention.

decisions.choice: I want (L, R); it is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} will (B); see (all levels)
decisions.reason: Literal and Readable say "I want", the plain word. Balanced says "it is my will" so that the authority in the verb is heard (meaning decision m3); "I will" is no longer clear in modern English. "See" is used for the verb of seeing; "behold" is no longer in use.

decisions.choice: all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} (B); {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} (R); before the world was founded (B), made (R)
alternatives: before the foundation of the world (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the neuter "all that", which ties the verse to 6:37 and 17:2 (meaning decision m1), and then "they". Readable turns it into a plain statement about the people given to Jesus. Both say "before the world was founded" or "made" for the noun phrase, which is plainer in English. Readable repeats "I want" and "this glory" to keep its sentences short.

decisions.choice: ce que tu m’as donné (L); ceux que tu m’as donnés (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the neuter singular of the SBLGNT, the believers seen as one whole (meaning decisions m1 and m2), and lets "eux" take up the persons, as the Greek does. Balanced names the persons at once, since French "ce que ... ils" is hard to follow aloud.

decisions.choice: 원합니다 for "I want"
decisions.reason: Jesus states his will here rather than making a request; 원하다 says that, where 바라다 would sound like a hope and 청하다 like the requests of verses 9-20.

decisions.choice: "what you have given me" stands first and alone, as in the Greek, and 그들 takes it up
decisions.reason: The neuter "what" sees the believers as one whole before "they" names them as persons; Literal keeps the break, Balanced and Readable smooth it.

source.text: Πάτερ δίκαιε, καὶ ὁ κόσμος σε οὐκ ἔγνω, ἐγὼ δέ σε ἔγνων, καὶ οὗτοι ἔγνωσαν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας, καὶ ἐγνώρισα αὐτοῖς τὸ ὄνομά σου καὶ γνωρίσω, ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ἣν ἠγάπησάς με ἐν αὐτοῖς ᾖ κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Father righteous, and the world you not knew, but I you knew, and these knew that you me sent; \v 26 and I made known to them the name of you and will make known, that the love [with] which you loved me in them may be, and I in them."

en.L: Righteous Father, the world indeed did not know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, but I knew {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and these knew that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \v 26 and I made known to them {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and I will make [it] known, so that the love with which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} may be in them, and I in them."
en.B: Righteous Father, even though the world has never known {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I have known {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and these disciples have come to know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 26 I have made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name known to them, and I will go on making it known, so that the love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have had for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} may be in them, and I in them."
en.R: Righteous Father, the world does not know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. But I know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and these disciples know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 26 I have made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name known to them. I have shown them who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are, and I will keep on doing it. Then the love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will be in them, and I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will be in them."

fr.L: Père juste, le monde, lui, ne {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a pas connu, mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai connu, et ceux-ci ont connu que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé ; \v 26 et je leur ai fait connaître {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, et je [le] ferai connaître, afin que l’amour avec lequel {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as aimé soit en eux, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en eux. »
fr.B: Père juste, même si le monde ne {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a jamais connu, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai connu, et ces disciples ont reconnu que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé. \v 26 Je leur ai fait connaître {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, et je continuerai à le faire connaître, pour que l’amour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} soit en eux, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en eux. »
fr.R: Père juste, le monde ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaît pas. Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connais, et ces disciples savent que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as envoyé. \v 26 Je leur ai fait connaître {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom. Je leur ai montré qui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es, et je vais continuer à le faire. Alors l’amour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} sera en eux, et {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, je serai en eux. »

vi.L: Lạy Cha công chính, thế gian đã không biết Cha, nhưng Con đã biết Cha, và những người này đã biết rằng Cha đã sai Con; \v 26 và Con đã cho họ biết danh Cha, và sẽ cho [họ] biết nữa, để tình yêu thương mà Cha đã yêu thương Con ở trong họ, và Con [cũng] ở trong họ."
vi.B: Lạy Cha công chính, dù thế gian chưa hề biết Cha, nhưng Con biết Cha, và các môn đồ này đã nhận biết rằng Cha đã sai Con. \v 26 Con đã cho họ biết danh Cha, và Con sẽ còn tiếp tục cho họ biết, để tình yêu thương Cha dành cho Con ở trong họ, và Con ở trong họ."
vi.R: Lạy Cha công chính, thế gian không biết Cha. Nhưng Con biết Cha, và các môn đồ này biết rằng Cha đã sai Con. \v 26 Con đã cho họ biết danh Cha. Con đã cho họ thấy Cha là ai, và Con sẽ còn tiếp tục làm như vậy. Rồi tình yêu thương Cha dành cho Con sẽ ở trong họ, và chính Con cũng sẽ ở trong họ."

ko.L: 의로우신 아버지, 세상은 아버지를 알지 못하였으나 저는 아버지를 알았고, 이들은 아버지께서 저를 보내신 것을 알았습니다. \v 26 그리고 저는 그들에게 아버지의 이름을 알렸고, 또 알릴 것입니다. 이는 아버지께서 저를 사랑하신 그 사랑이 그들 안에 있고, 저도 그들 안에 있게 하려는 것입니다."
ko.B: 의로우신 아버지, 세상은 아버지를 알지 못했지만 저는 아버지를 알았고, 이 제자들도 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 알게 되었습니다. \v 26 저는 아버지의 이름을 그들에게 알렸고, 앞으로도 계속 알리겠습니다. 그것은 아버지께서 저를 사랑하신 그 사랑이 그들 안에 있고, 저도 그들 안에 있게 하려는 것입니다."
ko.R: 의로우신 아버지, 세상은 아버지를 알지 못합니다. 그러나 저는 아버지를 압니다. 그리고 이 제자들은 아버지께서 저를 보내셨다는 것을 압니다. \v 26 저는 그들에게 아버지의 이름을 알려 주었습니다. 아버지께서 어떤 분이신지 보여 주었고, 앞으로도 계속 그렇게 하겠습니다. 그러면 아버지께서 저를 사랑하시는 그 사랑이 그들 안에 있을 것이고, 저도 그들 안에 있을 것입니다."

alignments.target_span: I will go on making it known

decisions.choice: Righteous Father: the Father who is just and does what is right, who judges between the world and those who know him
decisions.reason: Jesus calls God "righteous Father" (Πάτερ δίκαιε) only here. It fits what follows: he sets the world, which has not known the Father, against himself and the disciples, who have, and calls on the Father as the righteous judge who will rightly tell the two apart (compare 5:30; 7:24). 1 John uses the same word for God, who is righteous to forgive (1 John 1:9), and for "Jesus Christ the righteous" (1 John 2:1).

decisions.choice: the opening "and" and the "but" set the world's not knowing over against Jesus's knowing: "though the world did not know you, I knew you"
alternatives: "and" joining this sentence to the prayer before it
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with καὶ and goes on with δέ. The pairing marks a contrast: on the one side the world, on the other Jesus and these disciples. The "and" may also carry the sense "indeed" or "even". The aorists "knew" look at the whole of the world's refusal and of Jesus's knowing, not at a single moment.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity that has refused to know God
alternatives: all people, without that sense of refusal
decisions.reason: Here, unlike 17:21 and 23, the world is the human world that has turned from God: it did not know the Word through whom it was made (1:10), and it hates Jesus and his disciples because it does not know the one who sent him (15:21; 16:3). "These" are the disciples, who have known that the Father sent him (17:8).

decisions.choice: your name: the Father himself as he has made himself known; made known in Jesus's life and teaching, and to be made known still
alternatives: the name as a word or title only
decisions.reason: "Name" stands for the person and character of the Father, as in 17:6 and 17:11-12. Jesus has made the Father known in all he has said and done (1:18; 14:9). "I will make it known" looks ahead: to his death and rising, where the Father's love is shown most fully, and to the Spirit, who will make Jesus's words known to the disciples (14:26; 16:13-15, 25).

decisions.choice: the purpose of making the name known: that the Father's love for the Son, and the Son himself, may be in the disciples
decisions.reason: Knowing the Father is not only knowing about him. The love with which the Father has loved the Son (3:35; 17:24) is to live in the disciples, and so is the Son himself. The prayer ends with "and I in them", the promise of 14:20 and 14:23 and of the vine and the branches (15:4-5).

decisions.choice: and I in them (L, B), and I myself will be in them (R): last at every level
alternatives: and that I may be in them
decisions.reason: The prayer ends on the words "and I in them", which Literal and Balanced keep as the Greek has them, without a verb; the Greek leaves no other natural wording for these closing words. Readable supplies the verb but keeps the clause last, so that the prayer still ends with Jesus in them.

decisions.choice: even though ... has never known ... have known ... have come to know (B); does not know, know (R); these disciples (B, R); go on making it known, keep on doing it (B, R); the love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have had for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} (B), the love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} (R)
decisions.reason: The aorist "knew" sums up a whole history (meaning decision m2), so Balanced uses the English perfect and Readable the plain present. Balanced says "even though" for the contrast marked by "and ... but". Balanced and Readable name "these" as the disciples, and say "go on making it known" for the future "will make known". Readable also explains "your name" as "who you are" (meaning decision m4). For "the love with which you loved me" Balanced says "the love you have had for me" and Readable "the love you have for me", since that love did not end (17:24).

decisions.choice: le monde, lui, ne t’a pas connu, mais moi, je t’ai connu (L); même si le monde ne t’a jamais connu, moi, je t’ai connu (B)
alternatives: et le monde ne t’a pas connu, mais moi je t’ai connu
decisions.reason: The opening "and" and the following "but" set the world's not knowing against Jesus's knowing (meaning decision m2). French marks the contrast with stressed pronouns ("lui", "moi") at Literal, and with "même si" at Balanced, as the English Balanced does with "even though".

decisions.choice: Lạy Cha công chính
alternatives: Lạy Cha là Đấng công chính
decisions.reason: "Công chính" is the adjective of the key term "sự công chính" (righteousness); "công bình" is the 1926 word.

decisions.choice: 의로우신 아버지 for "Righteous Father"
decisions.reason: 의 is the guide's key term for righteousness; the honorific -시- belongs to an address to God.
